text:
Sam W: Heads up — BridgeFlow wants to run a 2-week joint POC next month. They want our co-sell badge and a shared roadmap doc.
Priya R: Nice. Do we have a proposed arch for tenant isolation + SSO?
Ethan L: Thinking: customer traffic goes to BridgeFlow frontend -> our hosted inference via partner routing policy. For enterprise accounts we can route to Dedicated pool.
Marta G: Q: will BridgeFlow provide SAML metadata or do we need them to use our IdP?
Sam W: They said SAML/SP-initiated. Ask them to send metadata by EOW.
Priya R: Also need to confirm who signs the security questionnaire — they expect a redwood security contact. @Ethan can you own that?
Ethan L: I can. I’ll attach our latest sec pack (SOC2 + data flow diagram) and the short answers.
Sam W: Pricing question from partner: for co-sell leads they want 10% partner margin on hosted usage and a discounted rate if they commit to 2TB embeddings per month. Thoughts?
Marta G: For hosted: we can offer a tiered volume discount after commit. For Dedicated, pricing is contract-level. We should ask revenue ops for a partner SKU.
Priya R: Action: Sales ops to propose partner SKU + margins. I’ll draft LOE for technical enablement.
Ethan L: Security Qs: they asked about key management, encryption at rest, and egress firewall rules. I’ll include our KMS integration notes and egress IP ranges.
Sam W: Network: BridgeFlow’s infra team asked about egress NAT IPs for allowlisting. @Jules (deploy-bot) can you paste the current hosted egress ranges?
Jules (deploy-bot): Hosted egress ranges: 52.23.120.0/22, 34.201.64.0/20. See internal link: https://intra.redwood/infra/egress-ranges
Marta G: Great. We also need to document telemetry: shared tracing header, and cost attribution tags so partner can bill their customers.
Priya R: Can we add a flag to pass partner_customer_id as a token-level metadata? Devex: is that feasible without exposing raw tokens?
Ethan L: Yes — we support metadata headers like `x-rw-partner-id`. We'll hook that into billing pipeline. Need engineering signoff on retention TTL.
Sam W: POC plan draft: Week 0: SSO + networking whitelists, Week 1: integration + basic generation tests, Week 2: load ramp + cost telemetry, postmortem + rollout playbook.
Marta G: Add a dedicated canary route for BridgeFlow traffic so we can rollback if performance dips.
Priya R: Enterprise blocker: BridgeFlow legal insists on a 30-day SLA for response times on incidents. We usually offer 72h for partners on co-sell trials. Need CS/Legal input.
Ethan L: Flagging legal. @Sam W can you loop in legal (legal@redwood) and CS to confirm SLA exceptions?
Sam W: Will do.
Marta G: For the POC we should propose a burnout test: 200 concurrent chats at 32 tokens/sec limit to validate KV cache and batching. Add memory/latency SLOs.
Ethan L: I’ll script a load job and share the `k6` scenario. Example snippet: ```k6 script here --vus 200 --duration 15m```
Priya R: BridgeFlow asked whether we can host model artifacts in their VPC for Private deployment. Is that supported?
Ethan L: Yes for Private: we can ship an on-prem package or configure our private control plane to run inside their VPC. That will need a longer lead time and an on-prem onboarding doc.
Sam W: OK owners: Ethan — sec questionnaire + load script, Priya — enablement LOE + runbook, Marta — billing tags + canary route, Sam — legal loop + partner SKU ask.
Marta G: Can we target an internal kickoff next Tue 10am PT with partner joining at 10:30?
Priya R: Calendar invite sent. Please add pre-read: architecture diagram + security one-pager.
Ethan L: I’ll upload the sec pack and `load-test` branch to the repo and link in the invite.
Sam W: Final ask: BridgeFlow wants a quick diagram showing failover to lower-cost model if Dedicated capacity is saturated. Can someone sketch that?
Marta G: I’ll do a one-slide fallback flow: Hosted -> Dedicated primary -> Fallback to quantized model in hosted region.
Priya R: Thanks team. I’ll follow up with partner thread and post updates here. :thumbsup:
